EARLIER RULINGS THAT STILL BIND AND ARE NOT RE-LITIGATED: F-1 this page is THE PLACE and /work/projects/farm-school is THE PROGRAMME; D-07.3 five acres and ninety minutes; F-5 Ladpuri; F-9 Mewat and the community; F-10 one tree, not none; F-11 the orchard as counts; F-14 no meal rates; F-16 the span is a derived bound, never a typed count; F-17 tents on the farm's own camping site; F-18 the participation figure lives on the work register and is RESOLVED from it here, never typed. top.lead: Five acres of barren ground at Ladpuri, in the Khairthal-Tijara district of Rajasthan — on the Haryana border, in the Mewat region, where the Aravallis run — ninety minutes from Delhi. One tree stood on it. It is now a Food Forest and a working farm, built with the people who live around it.
top._lead: AD-27.30. 'The Mewat country' is gone: the client read it as a nation, and the archaic sense (hill country, sheep country) is not worth the misreading. The district is added here and the rail label below carries it too. Khairthal-Tijara is the Rajasthan district formed out of the erstwhile Alwar district, which is the client's own qualifier; it is gated both ways in the build.

place.map_label: Where it is, on the map

The coordinates are in the record — 2026-08-22-FARM-source-ledger.md §2.1, from the farm's own Google listing — and google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query= is Google's documented URL API, so this link is CONSTRUCTED FROM A RECORDED FACT USING A PUBLISHED INTERFACE rather than guessed. origin.head:
A story of
change
origin.lead: One tree became more than five thousand, in less than {{lessthan}} years. Nothing here was improved. It was made, out of ground that had stopped being able to make anything.
origin.quote: So it's a story of transformation.
origin._: AD-27.32. The page's strongest number was the only one not set as a number: it sat inside row 1 of seven as running text, on a page that sets '20 Cows' as a 42px numeral two bands later. It is now the band's figure rail, and the Executive Director's sentence is promoted into the pull-quote it always was. Rows 2-7 moved to `built`; row 7 ('And it is not finished') is deleted and its content survives in `built`'s lead.

rail.label: Tree, when the land was bought
Trees now, most of them native
Years between the two
rail.period: derived from the year the land was bought

context.h: Where this is, and why it counts double
context.p: It sits in the Aravallis — the oldest range in India, running from the edge of Delhi down into Gujarat, and presently quarried, mined and built on. And it sits in the Mewat region, which is among the poorest in the country: the district on the Haryana side has ranked at the very bottom of the national development tables. The farm itself is on the Rajasthan side, in Khairthal-Tijara, carved out of the erstwhile Alwar district. Five restored acres in a comfortable place is landscaping. Here it is an argument.

frame.alt: Bare ground and low scrub at the edge of the farm, hills on the horizon

built.head:
Built by
Mewat
built.lead: The labour, the knowledge of what this ground does in June, and the hands that put the mud houses up are local. The people here are not beneficiaries; they are the reason there is anything to visit.

frame.alt: Four people working along freshly drawn furrows, sowing by hand

rows.p: Over five thousand, most of them native, because a native tree is the one the birds and insects here already know what to do with. Then shade, leaf litter, soil, and the birds.

rows.h: Permaculture, which here means the farm feeds itself
rows.p: Not a style of gardening. It is the rule that every output has to be some other part's input: leaves and dung into the vermicompost lab and out as soil, flowers into honey, fodder into milk.

rows.h: Mud houses, built out of the site itself
rows.p: Thatch over mud, with bottle glass set into the walls for light. Not a rustic effect — a prototype, tested by people sleeping in them through an Aravalli summer and an Aravalli January.

grows.head:
What grows
there now
grows.lead: The inventory is the evidence. A barren field does not have a manifest, and everything in this one had to be put there and kept alive.

figures.label: Trees, most of them native
figures.period: counted August 2026, from one tree at acquisition

figures.label: Saplings in the native nursery
figures.period: standing stock, no start year sourced

resolved.label: Dead leaves composted into soil on site

produce.h: What five barren acres put on a table
produce.p: Vegetables and leafy greens from the beds, oranges and lemons, turmeric, microgreens under racks, honey from the hives and milk from the herd. Most of what the kitchen puts in front of a group grew within sight of where they eat it.

frame.alt: Oranges ripening in dense clusters on the tree

systems.head:
{{systems}} things
running
systems._head: THE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED. AD-27.31 named this band 'Thirteen things running', which was the inventory's length before AD-27.33 moved solar into it; it is fourteen now. A typed numeral in a heading over a list is the easiest thing on this page to make false with one edit, so the build counts the list and writes the word. Add a system and the heading follows it.
systems.lead: Everything here is a system that has to produce. If one stops producing it stops teaching, and it gets fixed rather than relabelled.

items.p: Layered rather than planted in rows — canopy, understorey, ground.
Grown to be eaten. The kitchen serves what the beds gave that week.
Twenty cows. The milk and ghee are theirs; the dung starts the compost.

frame.alt: Cows on open ground at sunrise in warm haze

items.p: Small, and part of the cycle rather than a unit of production.
Twenty thousand saplings, which is why the tree count keeps going up.

frame.alt: Young plants at knee height in a nursery bed

items.p: Leaves and dung in at one end, soil out at the other.
Hives that have to be worked, not watched. Honey is the by-product.

frame.alt: A honeybee feeding on a mustard flower in full bloom

items.p: Planted for the insects, which is why it is best when it looks untidy.
Fodder grown without soil, for the months when nothing green grows outside.
Built to be lived in and watched. A prototype nobody sleeps in is untested.
Tents, and room for a hundred of them — hence campground, not guest house.
Drilled blocks and hollow stems, for the pollinators that do not live in hives.
Things taken apart and made into other things, rather than thrown away.

items.h: Solar, and an honest amount of it
items.p: Enough to matter, not enough to pretend the grid is not there. An inverter carries the rest.

systems._items: AD-27.33 deleted the band 'How the place keeps itself' entirely. Two of its three rows were restatements — water caught where it falls is `built` row 1, waste as raw material is `built` row 3 plus Vermicompost here — and only solar was unique. It is the last line above. Nothing sourced was lost and 111 words went.

visit.head:
Live, Learn,
Lead
visit.lead: The farm's own three words, and also the three lengths of stay: Learn is a day, Live is a night, Lead is what educators or a small organisation come to do with the rest of it.

triad.p: A night on the farm, in a mud house or a tent, with the crickets going.
Farming, food, water and waste, taught by a place that has to actually produce.
Educators and small organisations, using five acres as the room they think in.

doors.name: Day visits, half a day or a whole one
doors.p: A bus and a packed lunch. Half a day is the commonest shape; a full day gets you the afternoon, when most of the farming happens.
doors.who: Schools, colleges, families and individuals — and educators on their own account.

frame.alt: Children seated on a red bench under a bamboo-and-thatch pavilion roof, potted plants hanging above an open-air classroom

ask.label: Bring a group for the day

doors._: AD-27.34’s pending swap, taken 23 August. The door held farm-plot-children-facilitator.jpg — a facilitator and a group standing in a field, which is a farm photograph but not a day-visit one. swechha-farm-thatch-pavilion-classroom.jpg (720×960, from the AD-27 photo manifest, catalogued by lane 2) is children already seated and working under the pavilion, which is what a day here actually looks like, and it reads better in the door’s tall crop than a landscape field shot. IT IS A SWAP, NOT AN ADDITION: build-farm-page.mjs gates at 7–12 photographs and this page sits at 12, so the frame it replaces is the one given up (AD-27.34).

doors.name: Overnight school camps
doors.p: A night changes what a day out can be. Up to a hundred students stay over in tents on the farm's own camping site, and the dark is genuinely dark.
doors.who: School groups staying over, up to a hundred at a time, under canvas.

frame.alt: The mud houses lit from inside after dark, their windows warm against the field

doors._: TWO FIGURES, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT KINDS. `capacity` is this page's own — 100 students, what the camping site holds. `resolved` is read out of farm-school.json — 30 school groups a year, what actually happens — so it cannot drift from the work register or from /impact. Capacity first, then track record: 'can hold' before 'has hosted' reads as a promise, the other way round reads as an excuse. THIS DOOR CARRIES THE BAND'S ONE PRIMARY BUTTON (AD-27.37).

doors.name: Retreats for small organisations
doors.p: There is a table under thatch with the field on three sides of it. Small organisations come for a day or two of their own work; the chores do not distinguish between a board and a school group.
doors.who: Teams and small organisations wanting the city to stop being the reference point.

frame.alt: An open pavilion under thatch, drapes tied back around a round table and chairs

doors.name: Stays and internships
doors.p: Weeks rather than hours. An internship should end with a person running part of this place unsupervised; a shorter stay is a mud house and a hand with the day's work.
doors.who: Interns and researchers from India and abroad, and anyone who wants to stay.

frame.alt: Inside an A-frame mud house — a bed under the bamboo apex, a small window at the far end

doors.name: Volunteering camps
doors.p: A camp where the point is the work: planting, weeding, building, clearing, and leaving the place measurably changed. It is the door most people who end up staying came through first.
doors.who: Colleges, corporate teams and individuals. Numbers are limited by the work there is that week.
doors._frame_note: NO PHOTOGRAPH, AND THAT IS W-18 RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. The page sits at the top of W-18's 7-12 band, so a fifth framed door makes 13 and fails the gate. The library holds no photograph of volunteering labour at all, so the door is text, and the first photograph of a shramdaan replaces this note.

doing.head:
What a group
actually does
doing.lead: None of this is laid on. It is the day's work, and a group joins it.

items.p: The butterfly garden, and what a food forest looks like from inside one.
Five thousand trees where there was one has made this a birding site.

items.h: Farming, with your hands in it
items.p: Sowing, weeding, harvesting whatever is ready. Forty people make a dent.
Unglamorous, enormously popular, and the fastest way to work out how big five acres is.

items.h: Food, from the ground it grew in
items.p: Cooked on the farm from what the beds gave that week.
Feeding them, and finding out what twenty animals need every day.

items.h: The hives, and what they are for
items.p: Bees teach what a monoculture costs without anybody having to say the word.
Leaves and dung in, soil out. The whole argument of the farm in one shed.
Ninety minutes from Delhi is far enough to get the sky back.
No traffic under it — for many visitors, the loudest quiet they have sat in.
Labour given, not bought — the same practice the Yamuna clean-ups run on.

plainly.head:
It is not
a hotel
plainly.lead: The part most places leave out.

frame.alt: A washroom built into a mud wall, a basin and dried grass in the alcove

rows.p: Agricultural land. An inverter keeps the lights on, but you will notice.

rows.h: A large group sleeps under canvas
rows.p: Mud houses take a family; a school camp takes the camping site, in tents.
Mobile data works. That is the whole provision, and for many the reason to come.
Drawn here and filtered for drinking; the nearest shop is a couple of kilometres away.
Cows, bees, birds, buffalo, goats and chickens, none arranged for visitors.

plainly._rows: AD-27.35 cut seven rows to five. 'The nearest shop is a couple of kilometres away' folded into the groundwater row as a clause and 'the food is what the farm grew' folded into the animals row. THE SHOP CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING: build-farm-page.mjs asserts that the word 'kilometres' appears exactly once on the page and only in the nearest-shop sentence. Delete the clause and that gate must be retired in the same commit.
plainly.quote: It's not a hotel, it's natural, it's rustic. It's a real farm.
plainly.quote_attr: Vimlendu Jha, on the farm's own listing

act.head: Come and see
act.lead: There is no booking form: every way of coming here is different enough that it starts with a conversation. Say which door you mean and roughly when.
act._phone: REMOVED ON THE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION, 22 August: 'Remove my phone number from the site.' Ruling F-2 said this page ends in a phone number and an email rather than a form; the phone half is superseded and the email half stands. The page still ends in a person, which was F-2's point. DO NOT RE-ADD A PERSONAL NUMBER, and the build refuses any tel: link.
act.email_note: For school camps, courses and retreats, which are arranged rather than booked.

This was swechhaindia@gmail.com, which violates data/about-people.json's email_policy ('Only @swechha.in addresses are published') — AD-25 §6 item 5 flagged it and could not reach this file. It is now the address every Ask on the site uses, and the gate /act already runs is run here too.

onward.p: The programme that runs here — the five C's, the courses, and what a stay is actually for.
The farm is one of the things Swechha does. The register is the rest of them.

acquired._: Owner, 22 August 2026: 'we had one tree when we bought it 4 years ago.' Four years back from 2026 is 2022. THE ELAPSED COUNT IS NEVER TYPED — the build derives it from this year, per D-09.5 ('no year count is typed anywhere, the count derives from the founding year'), which is why 'four years' does not go stale in January. The year itself is a derivation from '4 years ago' and is worth the owner's confirmation.

Gone from this file: the `works` band ('How the place keeps itself' — heading, lead and rows 1-2, ~90 words, restatements of what is now `built` rows 1 and 3 and the Vermicompost inventory line; row 3, solar, survives as an inventory line). The `sheet` band ('The nursery, the hives, the herd' — heading, lead and note, 59 words carrying no fact; its three photographs survive, now beside the inventory cells they depict). `origin` row 7, 'And it is not finished' (~45 words; its content survives in `built`'s lead). The produce paragraph's opening clause (~40 words; the four orchard counts survive as figures in `grows`). `plainly` rows 5 and 6 as standalone rows (~50 words; both fold into surviving rows as clauses). Prose above the two-sentence cap in each of the five doors and eleven activities (~430 words). The word 'country' in the masthead standfirst. The `waiting` band, which had been empty since F-13 and F-18 closed its two claims — nothing on this page is unsourced, so there is no hole to name; hole() is still exported by the shell the day there is one. NOTHING SOURCED IS DELETED: every figure, every named system, every activity and all five doors survive.
_retracted: OWNER RETRACTION, 23 AUGUST 2026 — DO NOT RESTORE. `built` row 1, 'Water first, before anything was planted' / 'Swales cut across the slope, bundhs to hold the runoff, ponds to keep it. On five acres in the Aravallis the limit is rarely soil — it is whether the rain that falls in three weeks is still there in March.' The owner read the built page and said of that row, verbatim: 'The following is not true in teh farm page, delete it from the root'. So it is gone from the DATA, not hidden in the template, and a build gate now fails if 'Water first', 'swale' or 'bundh' returns to this page. The succession now reads trees -> permaculture -> mud houses, and `built`'s lead ('A Food Forest is a succession, and this is the order it went in') is still true of the three rows that remain. UPDATE, 23 August 2026 — HE RULED ON THE REST, SO THIS IS NOW SITE-WIDE. The same water-harvesting claim is ALSO in SOURCE-FACTS §72, sourced to Swechha's own 'Introduction to Swechha' PDF p8-9, and it also rendered on /work/projects/farm-school ('water harvesting in swales, bundhs and ponds'). His first instruction named the FARM page only, so that sentence was LEFT STANDING AND FLAGGED TO HIM rather than deleted on inference — which was the right call and produced the ruling. Asked directly, he said: 'delete the water swales and bundhs part'. THE CLAIM IS NOW RETRACTED EVERYWHERE, data/work/projects/farm-school.json included, and §72 carries the ruling. The PDF still says it; the site does not, because the owner — who runs the farm — says it is not what is on the ground. Do not restore it on any page on the strength of the PDF; that would need a new statement from him.
